The Terraform behind this week

week-08-log-analytics — what each file does, and how big it actually is
week-08-log-analytics/
│
├── terraform/
│   ├── versions.tf          36   # azurerm + azapi, and the HCP backend
│   ├── variables.tf         29   # subscription, location, daily cap, alert email
│   ├── main.tf             145   # the workspace, and the two custom tables on
│   │                             # deliberately different PLANS
│   ├── ingestion.tf        164   # endpoint, collection rule, the TRANSFORM, the
│   │                             # alert rule, and who may write into it
│   └── outputs.tf           18   # workspace id and the ingestion URL
│
└── scripts/
    ├── deploy.sh            52   # registers two providers, then applies
    ├── validate.sh         162   # 5 checks. #4 sends 100 rows and counts what
    │                             # survived - the only way to know a filter filters
    └── cleanup.sh           46   # REFUSES without --force: this week stays up

# 9 resources, and the split follows the two questions
#
# main.tf answers "where does the data land, and how is it priced" -- the
# workspace, its cap, and the table plans.
#
# ingestion.tf answers "what gets in, and who is told when it stops" -- the
# endpoint, the rule, the one line of KQL that drops rows before they are
# billed, the alert on the cap, and a role assignment scoped to the rule
# rather than the resource group.
#
# Changing what data costs is a main.tf change. Changing what arrives is an
# ingestion.tf change. They are rarely the same decision.
